subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan (MAP) - final sign-off / go-live readiness
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: MAP draft + post-demo next steps (ACME)

Hi John 

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the mutual action plan (MAP) draft and recommended milestones so we have clarity on responsibilities and the target close/go-live timeline. I attached ACME_Redwood_MAP_v3.xlsx with the line-item milestones. High level: 

- Goal: Pilot Redwood inference on ACME's customer support pipeline, target go-live for pilot: 2026-05-04
- Success criteria: 10% reduction in median response time, and F1 >= 0.72 on the intent classifier within pilot window
- Key milestones (owner / target date):
  1) Procure test dataset & access (ACME) / due 2026-03-26
  2) Provision dedicated test capacity (Redwood infra) / due 2026-03-30
  3) Integration & API keys + initial verification tests (ACME + Redwood) / due 2026-04-10
  4) Quality tuning & evals (joint) / due 2026-04-24
  5) Pilot go-live & monitoring (ACME) / target 2026-05-04

Dependencies we called out: data access (SFTP or secure Drive), legal review of data handling (ACME legal), and SOW sign-off for dedicated capacity.

Ask: Can you confirm the dataset ownership and a single point of contact on your side for dataset delivery? Once that's confirmed we'll lock in provisioning dates and share the SOW draft.

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP draft)

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa  good recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: Priya (cc'd) will own dataset delivery. We can provide a sanitized export by 2026-03-25 via secure Drive. Confirmed.
2) Sizing/Capacity: Can you confirm the expected GPU footprint for the pilot (rough estimate) so procurement can plan costs?
3) Legal/SOW: Our procurement/legal team will need a draft SOW to start redlines. Can you loop in pricing and the committed throughput numbers?

Also  for the success criteria, can you clarify the evaluation window (2 weeks after go-live?) and what metrics Redwood will instrument vs ACME?

John

Hi John  great, thanks for confirming dataset ownership. Quick answers inline: 

- GPU footprint: For the pilot profile you described (bursty customer support inference, ~50 qps peak, average seq len 150), initial reserved capacity estimate is 2x A10-like GPUs (dedicated pool). Logan will follow up with a more precise sizing doc and cost estimate this afternoon.
- Evaluation window: we suggest 2 weeks stabilization after pilot go-live, with joint checkpoints at day 3, day 7, and day 14. Redwood will provide token-level latency/cost dashboards and model-quality evals; ACME should provide ground-truth labels for the evaluation window.
- SOW & Pricing: Attached is ACME_SOW_draft_20260319.pdf with the committed throughput and pricing bands. Please send procurement contact details for redline.

I uploaded an updated MAP (v3) that includes your dataset owner and the sizing notes; see attached. If the plan looks good, can you confirm target close/signature by 2026-04-01 so we can reserve the Dedicated capacity for your pilot window?

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_MAP_v3.xlsx, ACME_SOW_draft_20260319.pdf

Thanks  I'll wait on Priya for dataset drop details.

Best,
Marissa

- Procurement: Logan will post the sizing/cost estimate to the Drive folder and add a brief breakdown for reserved vs burst capacity.

I also uploaded a signature-ready copy of the agreement: RDW-Signature-Ready-Agreement.pdf. That is our standard template; Rachel can accept minor redlines but any changes to SLAs or data residency will need leadership approval.
